q: Is trimethoprim still a good choice for urine infections here?

blocks.md: For E. coli urine results, **20% were trimethoprim-resistant** in the latest year; that is lab susceptibility data, not treatment success.

This covers the first E. coli urine isolate per patient, not every urine infection or organism. Check the patient’s culture results; these data alone do not establish whether trimethoprim is a good choice for an individual.

blocks.md: For first **E. coli urine isolates**, resistant-result counts rose for trimethoprim (483 to 509) while tested samples fell from 2,592 to 2,544.

blocks.md: For **E. coli urine results**, resistance to ciprofloxacin no longer shows the earlier difference in how often trimethoprim resistance also occurs.

The recent figures show that 20% of results resistant to ciprofloxacin were also resistant to trimethoprim, compared with 20% when ciprofloxacin worked. This describes linked lab resistance, not treatment outcomes.

blocks.md: **Yes, for E. coli in urine**, resistance differed by sex for some drugs; age group differences were unclear.
For ciprofloxacin, resistance was 6% in women and 13% in men; clear differences also appeared for ampicillin, cefuroxime, and ceftriaxone. No age group difference was clear for the drugs shown.
